text: REST APIs are a common way for applications to communicate over the internet. When designing them, you should create clear endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API. It is also important to use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these best practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and improve over time.
